newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on selective selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on selective selling.

text.p: Shanghai B shares closed down on Tuesday on selling of stocks that posted poor interim results, brokers said.
The index fell 0.089 points or 0.17 percent to 51.492 points, on volume of 10.7 million shares worth $4.2 million. Of 41 B shares, 34 traded, with 10 down, 16 flat and eight up.
Brokers said that overseas selling of stocks that posted poor results had depressed the index recently.
"Many stocks reported very poor interim results, which triggered heavy overseas selling," one broker said.
"The index will continue to consolidate around 51/52 points, with short-term adjustment of individual stocks in the short term," a second broker said.
Shanghai Vacuum and Electron Devices was the biggest loser on poor interim results, tumbling $0.012 or 8.45 percent to $0.130, on volume of 287,000 shares.

Tientsin Marine bucked the market trend, on expectations of good net profits because of its container business. It traded the most, gaining $0.002 or 0.59 percent to $0.336, on volume of 1.9 million shares.
Shanghai A share index fell late in the session, with most players switching to the Shenzhen bourse, brokers said.

The A index shed 4.853 points or 0.58 percent to 836.739 points, on volume of 337.4 million shares worth 2.7 billion yuan. The SSE 30 index ended down 11.056 points or 0.51 percent to 2137.491 points.
Shanghai Fello was the biggest loser, falling 0.34 yuan or 5.00 percent to 6.46 yuan, on volume of 957,524 shares.
